feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
entry.summary:
Player-1 is a post-training framework that uses synthetic experience and PPO reinforcement learning to significantly improve computer-use agent performance across complex 2D and 3D games.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that training agents in synthetic, procedurally randomized environments with composite action spaces enables broad zero-shot transfer to complex, unseen interactive visual environments.

entry.title: RuleTrek: Benchmarking Agentic Rule Reasoning in Complex Scenarios
entry.summary:
RuleTrek is a new multi-domain benchmark that evaluates agentic rule reasoning across complex, multi-file scenarios in interactive workspaces.

Why it matters: It reveals that state-of-the-art LLM agents struggle to identify and deductively apply domain-specific rules when factual information is distributed across complex file environments.

entry.title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
entry.summary:
Cortex internalizes context-induced performance gains into LLM parametric memory using query generation and mergeable low-rank or structural FFN updates without losing non-target capabilities.

Why it matters: It enables large language models to permanently retain new skills and factual edits from context without requiring perpetual context window usage or degrading base model capabilities.

entry.title: ActionOPD: Distilling Decisions, Not Tokens
entry.summary:
ActionOPD is an action-level, on-policy distillation method that aligns student model decisions with black-box teacher decisions using semantic action agreement rewards instead of token-level probabilities.

Why it matters: It enables effective distillation of proprietary, black-box, or cross-tokenizer teacher models into smaller student agents without forcing the student to imitate teacher reasoning tokens.

entry.title: Apertus 1.5: From Open Text Models to Open Multimodal Reasoners
entry.summary:
Apertus 1.5 extends open text models to multimodal reasoning via continued pretraining, expanding context windows to 262k tokens and adding image and audio understanding without changing the base LM architecture.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that competitive multimodal reasoning models with 262k context windows can be built and fully open-sourced using strictly permissive data and transparent training recipes.

entry.title: KV4-RL: Unlocking Faster Asynchronous Rollouts for RLVR with INT4 KV Cache Quantization
entry.summary:
KV4-RL accelerates RLVR asynchronous rollouts using INT4 KV cache quantization paired with selective INT8 protection for attention sinks and recent context.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces memory bandwidth bottlenecks and generation latency in RLVR training without degrading downstream model accuracy.

entry.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
entry.summary:
HybridAgents dynamically switch between text interaction and latent space reasoning within a single unified generation process, supported by a lightweight HybridLink component and specialized SFT and RL post-training algorithms.

Why it matters: This approach enables LLM agents to execute fast, cost-effective internal latent reasoning without sacrificing text-based tool integration or interpretability.

entry.title: τ-Emotion-Bench: Exposing the Interaction Fragility of LLM Agents through Real-World User Emotions
entry.summary:
τ-Emotion-Bench evaluates tool-calling LLM agents across ten domains using emotion-conditioned user interactions, while the Tracer pipeline generates interaction-aware training trajectories.

Why it matters: It provides a framework to measure and improve agent reliability in real-world deployments where human users exhibit uncooperative or emotional behavior.

entry.title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
entry.summary:
SwarmRSI is a framework that enables scientific agent swarms to achieve recursive self-improvement by mutating and recombining research hypotheses and program components based on experimental feedback.

Why it matters: It enables multi-agent systems to leverage partial results and cross-agent feedback to autonomously evolve actionable scientific hypotheses and reproducible software implementations.

entry.title: SkillMarker: A KGW-Based Watermarking Method for Agent Skill Ownership Verification
entry.summary:
SkillMarker adapts the KGW watermarking algorithm to agent skills by combining quality-constrained rewriting with signal-oriented candidate search to protect intellectual property.

Why it matters: It enables robust IP protection and leakage tracing for structured AI agent skills without degrading their factual or procedural operational execution.

entry.title: Efficient Scene-Text Refinement via Pixel-Space Grouped Image Generation
entry.summary:
PixText introduces pixel-space grouped image generation for scene-text refinement, using MeanFlow to achieve high OCR accuracy and unedited content preservation in four steps.

Why it matters: It enables fast, highly accurate local text corrections in generated images without degrading surrounding visual context or introducing latent reconstruction artifacts.

entry.title: ProgAgent: Learning Tool Orchestration through Programmatic Training
entry.summary:
ProgAgent introduces a programmatic tool calling (PTC) training stack—comprising synthetic task generation, a lightweight runtime, and a two-stage training recipe—that trains agents to execute tools via code rather than sequential tool invocations.

Why it matters: PTC-based training enables large language models to maintain performance over long-horizon tasks and massive environment contexts where traditional direct tool calling fails.

entry.title: The Thinking Leakage in Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
entry.summary:
A study on Qwen3 models trained via GRPO reveals that reasoning gains in NO-THINK mode stem from thinking leakage, which reactivates the original model's existing THINK-mode abilities rather than learning novel reasoning behaviors.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that RL gains in non-reasoning modes may merely unmask pre-existing reasoning capabilities rather than teach models genuinely new reasoning mechanisms.

entry.title: SafeDriveVLA: Navigation-Conditioned World Model Dreaming for Conflict-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving
entry.summary:
SafeDriveVLA introduces navigation-conditioned world model dreaming and explicit compliance-mode prediction to handle conflicting and adversarial natural-language navigation instructions safely.

Why it matters: It improves the safety and adversarial robustness of open-ended vision-language-action driving models when facing driver error or malicious natural-language commands.

entry.title: VITAL: From Visual Motion to Precise Action
entry.summary:
VITAL introduces an action tokenizer that combines a visually derived motion scaffold with a compact residual, enabling precise autonomous vehicle trajectory prediction via flow matching in a single denoising step.

Why it matters: It bridges the gap between visual motion anticipation and precise control, delivering state-of-the-art driving performance at significantly higher inference speeds.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
entry.summary:
CoPE introduces multi-step action targets to agentic RL, training a single shared policy backbone to co-evolve acting and forecasting on successful trajectories without added inference overhead.

Why it matters: It significantly improves language agent sample efficiency and trajectory performance by utilizing intermediate step supervision without incurring extra runtime costs.

entry.title: Continuum Attention
entry.summary:
Continuum Attention replaces discrete key-value lookups in Transformer decoders with continuous piecewise linear memory curve integration, evaluating exact normalized attention via closed-form exponential moments.

Why it matters: Continuum Attention introduces mathematically exact continuous integration as a superior-performing mathematical replacement for discrete key-value lookups in Transformer attention mechanisms.

entry.title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
CriticOPD restores teacher recoverability during on-policy distillation by having the teacher critique student errors, enabling the student to train on successful revisions generated without privileged critique information.

Why it matters: It improves token-level teacher supervision on incorrect rollouts, allowing student models to effectively learn error correction and achieve higher reasoning accuracy on complex tasks.

entry.title: VASPO: Self-Distillation with Privileged Value Estimation
entry.summary:
VASPO integrates privileged self-distillation with PPO by combining token-level critic value estimates with self-teacher probability ratio modulation on student-generated prefixes.

Why it matters: VASPO demonstrates that leveraging privileged information through both the critic and teacher within PPO yields superior reasoning performance compared to combining self-teacher signals with GRPO.

entry.title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling
entry.summary:
Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR) provides token-level credit assignment from a single trajectory by computing Jensen-Shannon divergence between causal and hindsight policy views.

Why it matters: HP-RLVR reduces computational costs by an order of magnitude while ensuring consistent gradient signals even when all sampled rollouts yield identical outcomes.

entry.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
entry.summary:
Latent Compaction uses test-time training to compress document KV caches up to 32x without updating model weights or requiring access to downstream questions.

Why it matters: Treating the KV cache as an optimizable neural network via test-time training significantly lowers memory overhead for long contexts while preserving downstream retrieval accuracy.

entry.title: Decoupled Marginal Sharpening for Training-Free Inference-Time Scaling
entry.summary:
Decoupled Marginal Sharpening (DMS) improves training-free inference-time scaling in LLMs by decoupling reasoning-path exploration from answer-marginal sharpening and sampling via Fully Adapted Annealed SMC.

Why it matters: It enables higher inference-time reasoning performance without requiring weight updates or external reward models.

entry.title: Training Language Models to Fail Gracefully
entry.summary:
GracefulRL uses outcome-level rewards to train language models to execute safe fallback policies when task completion is unreliable, avoiding overconfidence without requiring inference-time verifiers or extra annotations.

Why it matters: By training models to fall back safely instead of guessing, GracefulRL reduces high-cost failure modes in downstream deployments like executing database queries or pushing code.

entry.title: MMLA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through RTT and RTMA
entry.summary:
MMLA-RSI is a recursive self-improvement framework using Reasoning-Time Training (RTT) and Reasoning-Time Memory Adaptation (RTMA) to update policy states and authoritative memory alongside their own adaptation methods.

Why it matters: It establishes formal execution bounds and mechanisms for agents to recursively self-improve both their operational states and their meta-learned update algorithms.

entry.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
entry.summary:
ReaDy is the first speculative decoding method that retrieves dynamic context from Hybrid Linear Attention (HLA) recurrent states using position-specific learned queries to accelerate LLM inference.

Why it matters: It improves speculative decoding efficiency and acceptance rates in hybrid linear attention models by repurposing compact recurrent states for dynamic context retrieval.

entry.title: Urbex: Agentic Spatial Grounding for City-Scale 3D Scenes
entry.summary:
Urbex is an agentic vision-language framework that replaces candidate ranking with active spatial search for candidate-free 3D grounding in city-scale scenes.

Why it matters: By eliminating precomputed candidate proposals, Urbex improves both speed and generalization for large-scale outdoor 3D visual grounding.

entry.title: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles
entry.summary:
Jeva is a decision-native System 1 model architecture that processes options independently via a shared encoder and compact decision stack to achieve permutation invariance, scalable candidate sets, cross-request caching, and explicit null detection.

Why it matters: It replaces text serialization in decision tasks with a native architecture that significantly reduces latency via option reuse and improves reliability through guaranteed permutation invariance and robust null detection.

entry.title: Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively
entry.summary:
Agent-Reflex is a three-stage training framework that teaches language agents proactive self-reflection, error recovery, and responsiveness to user corrections in noisy tool environments.

Why it matters: It improves the robustness and recovery capabilities of LLM agents operating in realistic, noisy environments with imperfect tool responses and real-time user interventions.

entry.title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
entry.summary:
VideoJev introduces a System One model family for video understanding that replaces autoregressive MLLM decoding with a unified scoring head for fast, structured decision-making.

Why it matters: VideoJev provides visual agents with a reusable, highly efficient decision interface that dramatically reduces latency for video grounding and question answering tasks.

entry.title: AesCode: Aesthetic Code Generation with Decoupled Cross-Modal Rewards
entry.summary:
AesCode uses decoupled cross-modal rewards and reference images to optimize code generation for visually rich artifacts like slides and dashboards.

Why it matters: It enables open-source models to generate editable, verifiable code that achieves visual design quality on par with top closed-source frontier models.

entry.title: Multics: Generative Multi-Player World Model with Hierarchical Communication
entry.summary:
Multics introduces a hierarchical communication framework using group and global tokens to scale multi-player generative world models to more players with lower computational complexity.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, real-time multi-agent interactive video generation without the quadratic computational overhead or event interference of prior fully-connected or centralized methods.

entry.title: EviScene: Beyond "Is It AI?" for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment
entry.summary:
EviScene introduces a multimodal ReAct agent and the EviLens benchmark to evaluate generic visual claim factuality beyond simple AI-generation detection.

Why it matters: It enables automated systems to verify the factual context of images through iterative retrieval and visual inspection rather than relying solely on deepfake detection.

entry.title: GreenWAM: A World Foundation Model for Robotics
entry.summary:
GreenWAM is a unified robot world foundation model trained across 20 robot families using a shared anatomical action space, performing state-of-the-art world prediction and competitive policy execution.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that a single generalized world model can simultaneously act as an accurate scene predictor and a robust control policy across vastly different robot architectures.

entry.title: Learning How to Remember: Memory Modality Selection for GUI Agents
entry.summary:
SwitchMem is a routing framework for vision-language model GUI agents that dynamically selects between textual and visual memory representations at each step based on step-dependent preferences.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that memory modality choice is step-dependent enables visual-language GUI agents to retrieve and use past interactions more effectively.

entry.title: VEDJE: Video-Efficient Discriminative Joint Encoder for Scalable Video-Text Retrieval
entry.summary:
VEDJE introduces a video-efficient discriminative joint encoder that compresses intra-frame video features into a reusable cache for fast, accurate video-text retrieval.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that high-accuracy video retrieval can be achieved using compact, pre-encoded visual features, significantly lowering computational and storage costs for dynamic search applications.

entry.title: FlashVSR+: Efficient Video Super-Resolution via Hybrid Attention and Reward-Yield Distribution Matching
entry.summary:
FlashVSR+ combines a spatial locality-focused hybrid attention architecture with Reward-Yield Distribution Matching Distillation (Ry-DMD) to enable efficient, preference-aligned, one-step video super-resolution.

Why it matters: It significantly lowers hardware barriers for high-resolution video restoration by running untiled 4K inference on consumer-grade GPUs while retaining alignment with human preferences.

entry.title: Self-Distillation with Verbal Regularization
entry.summary:
Self-Distillation with Verbal Regularization (VRSD) uses system prompts to mitigate teacher shortcuts and entropy drops caused by privileged information during on-policy self-distillation.

Why it matters: VRSD prevents premature optimization and shortcut reasoning in teacher models, leading to higher quality self-distillation supervision for complex reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Data-Centric Recursive Self-Improvement for Navigation via Policy-Synchronized Language-Action Dual Bootstrapping
entry.summary:
RSI-Nav introduces a data-centric recursive self-improvement framework for navigation that unifies instruction-following and instruction-generation in a shared model using policy-synchronized, shard-wise online data bootstrapping.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need for costly human annotations and separate auxiliary models by allowing navigation agents to self-improve through synchronized data generation and policy updates.

entry.title: A Decade in a Day: Synthesizing Agent-Native Interfaces from Human-Oriented Software Evolution
entry.summary:
Researchers created DeskIF-Bench to study how software interface evolution impacts AI agents, leading to ANIS, a framework that synthesizes agent-native interfaces to boost task success while dramatically reducing token consumption.

Why it matters: Synthesizing tailored, agent-native interfaces instead of relying on human visual UIs or complex SDKs significantly improves LLM agent execution accuracy while reducing operational token costs.

entry.title: Open-o3-Video-v2: Seek, Ground, and Reason with Verifiable Spatio-Temporal Evidence
entry.summary:
Open-o3-Video-v2 introduces an agentic spatio-temporal reasoning framework that dynamically retrieves, grounds, and verifies object-level visual evidence within reasoning trajectories.

Why it matters: It improves reliability and interpretability in long-video understanding by allowing models to actively seek out missing video evidence and verify claims with object-level temporal grounding.

entry.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
entry.summary:
DoubtLess is a training-free contrastive decoding method that uses a smaller reasoning model's logit differences, driven by brief versus verbose prompts, to shorten large model chains-of-thought without sacrificing accuracy.

Why it matters: It enables significant inference-cost and latency reductions for long chain-of-thought reasoning models without requiring expensive model retraining or suffering accuracy degradation.

entry.title: Beyond the Verdict: Agentic Code Judging with Verifiable Feedback
entry.summary:
Researchers created USACO-JUDGE and trained ARBITER, a 35B MoE agentic verifier, using RL in an execution sandbox to judge code correctness and generate verifiable counterexamples without official judging systems.

Why it matters: ARBITER enables accurate test-time scaling, code selection, and automated refinement by generating verifiable execution feedback without exhausting official submission limits.

entry.title: PreciseCoder: Faithful and Generalizable Debugging Beyond Unit-Test Rewards
entry.summary:
PreciseCoder augments unit-test RL rewards with a signal for semantically verified, localized edits, preventing models from hallucinating bugs and reducing edit sizes while maintaining high pass rates.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that localizing rewards to specific edit locations prevents code over-editing and bug hallucination, producing concise, transferable bug-fixing reasoning for larger models.

entry.title: Unlocking Token Rewards via Training-Free Reward Attribution
entry.summary:
A training-free method, P2T, extracts token-level reward signals from process reward models using a first-order Taylor approximation requiring only one forward and backward pass.

Why it matters: It enables precise token-level credit assignment for reinforcement learning algorithms without the computational burden of N forward passes or training specialized token-level reward models.

entry.title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
ProAS introduces a critic-free framework that uses an Agentic Reference Graph to fix uniform credit assignment in multi-turn LLM agent reinforcement learning via action masking and asymmetric penalty redistribution.

Why it matters: It improves task success rates and training efficiency for multi-turn LLM agents without the computational memory overhead of maintaining a separate critic model.

entry.title: Geometric Calibration of Supervised Fine-Tuning
entry.summary:
SPACE is a data-free, post-hoc calibration method that mitigates out-of-domain knowledge regression by reverting supervised fine-tuning weight updates within the principal subspace of pre-SFT weights.

Why it matters: It provides an efficient, training-free way to reduce out-of-domain performance degradation while simultaneously improving in-domain results after supervised fine-tuning.

entry.title: Can an Agent Learn to Predict Its Own Failure? Outcome-Grounded Confidence Calibration in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
A novel RL training approach uses Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and proper scoring rules to calibrate an LLM agent's per-step verbalized confidence against eventual multi-step episode outcomes rather than immediate step correctness.

Why it matters: Enabling agents to accurately predict overall task failure from early steps allows for safer automated deployment through reliable selective execution, abstention, or human handoff.

entry.title: Does self-distillation improve reasoning?
entry.summary:
A systematic evaluation shows self-distillation methods like SDPO and OPSD fail to consistently improve reasoning generalization, with performance gains driven by overfitting rather than effective use of privileged information.

Why it matters: The findings challenge the assumption that self-distillation is a superior alternative to reinforcement learning for complex reasoning, highlighting the need for better techniques to leverage privileged information.

entry.title: DPOison-VL: Clean Preference Poisoning in Vision-Language Direct Preference Optimization
entry.summary:
DPOison-VL is the first clean preference poisoning attack against vision-language DPO, using imperceptible image perturbations on just 2% of training data to manipulate alignment with up to 98% attack success rate.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that multimodal preference alignment can be covertly hijacked through visually imperceptible image perturbations without altering prompts, text responses, or preference labels.

entry.title: Beyond Answer Voting: Fine-Grained Correction of LLM Reasoning through Graph Alignment across Sampled Traces
entry.summary:
DDRG improves LLM multi-step reasoning by aligning sampled reasoning traces into claim graphs to detect intermediate conflicts and apply localized repairs without expanding the initial sample bank.

Why it matters: It enables fine-grained, claim-level error correction in LLM reasoning chains using existing trace samples without requiring additional compute to expand the candidate pool.

entry.title: AgentSWE: Can Coding Agents Build the Agent You Actually Want?
entry.summary:
AgentSWE is a new benchmark featuring 25 tasks designed to evaluate coding agents across three stages of building custom agents: Creation, Editing, and Optimization.

Why it matters: The benchmark demonstrates that current coding agents reliably fail to build functional, requirement-compliant custom agents, highlighting a critical gap between apparent code completion and actual operational reliability.

entry.title: Scaling Agentic Data for Long-Horizon Terminal Intelligence
entry.summary:
Researchers developed TerminalHorizon, an automated data synthesis engine for long-horizon terminal agents, and fine-tuned Qwen3.5-27B to achieve performance gains across 12 benchmarks.

Why it matters: Automating the generation of high-quality, long-horizon trajectory data enables LLM agents to perform sustained autonomous work and complex, multi-stage problem solving in real-world professional environments.

entry.title: Thinking Inertia: LLMs Keep Thinking When Told Not To
entry.summary:
Researchers identify 'Thinking Inertia' in LLMs, showing that explicit inference persists under strict no-thinking prompt controls, particularly as answer spaces become more open-ended.

Why it matters: System instruction controls or model settings alone are insufficient to guarantee that LLMs suppress internal explicit reasoning, requiring specialized evaluation frameworks.

entry.title: Multi-Stream Attention Residuals
entry.summary:
Multi-Stream Attention Residuals generalizes depth-wise attention to multi-head streams using multi-scale causal convolutions and adaptive mixing, outperforming prior residual architectures in large-scale model pre-training efficiency.

Why it matters: MSAR offers a more compute-efficient residual architecture for large-scale pre-training, achieving significantly faster convergence for LLMs and MoE models at equivalent loss targets.

entry.title: Humanity's Sixth Sense: Benchmarking Intuitive Visual Reasoning in Multimodal Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Humanity's Sixth Sense (HSS), a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on intuitive, implicit visual reasoning across temporal, spatial, social, and abstract domains.

Why it matters: The benchmark reveals a critical capability gap where frontier multimodal models struggle with zero-shot visual intuition that humans perform effortlessly, highlighting a limitation in current model scaling.

entry.title: When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better
entry.summary:
Semi-OPD distills teachers into students using initial student rollouts, outperforming on-policy distillation in accuracy and efficiency unless teacher and student outputs are highly aligned.

Why it matters: Practitioners can significantly reduce training time and improve model accuracy by substituting complex on-policy distillation with offline initial student rollouts for misaligned model pairs.

entry.title: SpatialASM: Internalizing Active Mentalization for Spatial Reasoning
entry.summary:
SpatialASM is a framework that internalizes Active Spatial Mentalization into LVLMs via training-time spatial simulation using an allocentric novel-view generator.

Why it matters: It provides a scalable data synthesis method to overcome the scarcity of spatial Chain-of-Thought supervision, improving spatial reasoning in vision-language models.

entry.title: Universal Textual Teaching for LLMs
entry.summary:
Universal Textual Teaching (UTT) is a parameter-update-free knowledge distillation framework that converts Teacher-Student knowledge gaps into a reusable natural-language prompt artifact called a Primer.

Why it matters: UTT enables effective knowledge distillation for black-box or API-only models without requiring expensive model retraining or architecture-specific parameter updates.

entry.title: Coding-Agent Benchmarks Should Match Their Users' Task Flows
entry.summary:
Researchers analyzed 4,782 real-world JetBrains IDE coding agent sessions to introduce SWE-TaskFlow, a method that aligns issue-derived benchmarks with realistic user interaction patterns.

Why it matters: Evaluating coding agents on static single-prompt issues fails to reflect real-world developer interactions, which directly impacts agent execution costs and functional performance.

entry.title: Systematic Multi-Agent Vision-and-Language Navigation: Formulation, Benchmark, and Method
entry.summary:
This paper formalizes Systematic Multi-Agent Vision-and-Language Navigation (MAVLN) under dependency and resource constraints, introducing a 11,724-episode benchmark and the TRISS navigation system.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized benchmark and architectural framework for coordinating teams of autonomous robots executing complex, multi-agent navigation tasks from natural language instructions.

entry.title: One Model to Loop Them All: Elastic Latent Recurrence for Language Models
entry.summary:
Elastic Latent Recurrence (ELR) trains latent recurrent language models that match non-recurrent baseline accuracy at a single loop while gaining substantial accuracy improvements with additional loops at inference.

Why it matters: ELR enables serving a single model checkpoint that dynamically trades off latency and compute for higher accuracy without paying a performance penalty at minimal loop counts.

entry.title: ARCS: Towards Precise Text-to-SQL via Structured Disambiguation
entry.summary:
ARCS introduces structured disambiguation for text-to-SQL tasks via constrained interactions alongside a benchmark annotated with real-world database ambiguities, interpretations, and SQL queries.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that standard text-to-SQL models fail frequently when facing real-world database ambiguities and offers a structured interaction framework to address these intent deviations.

entry.title: Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training
entry.summary:
An uncertainty-guided progressive contraction framework compresses chain-of-thought post-training supervision by using Monte Carlo reasoning trees and online student-aware routing to maintain performance using 0.22% of the optimization budget.

Why it matters: This approach significantly cuts computational costs for reasoning post-training by replacing massive static dataset training with dynamic, uncertainty-driven data filtering.

entry.title: Mental-Models for Multi-Agent Systems
entry.summary:
A new framework equips multi-agent systems with an amortized recursive Theory-of-Mind mental model, enabling agents to infer counterpart states and condition policy decisions on explicit partner representations.

Why it matters: Explicitly modeling a partner's latent beliefs and intentions provides a structured inductive bias that improves decision-making in multi-agent environments under partial observability.

entry.title: Less from More: Reinforcing Sparse Video Reasoning from Dense References
entry.summary:
SAVER is a dense-to-sparse post-training framework that uses reinforcement learning on dense video references to train models to reason accurately using sparse temporal evidence.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that targeted temporal grounding training allows models to achieve state-of-the-art video understanding accuracy with significantly lower computational and frame overhead.

entry.title: Pretraining and Test-Time Training Budgets Matter for ARC: A Controlled Study of VARC and TRM
entry.summary:
A controlled study on ARC-AGI-1 evaluates VARC and TRM across five pretraining and four test-time training (TTT) budgets, showing distinct performance responses to data scaling.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that ARC model performance relies heavily on pretraining and TTT scaling highlights the need to report and compare ARC architectures under standardized compute and data budgets.

entry.title: Constructing Pareto Frontiers of Optimal Reasoning Termination Methods for Overthinking in Reasoning Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Step-wise Truncation Probing, defined overthinking metrics, unified reasoning termination strategies into a Pareto frontier framework, and released OTBench using 70.5 billion reasoning tokens across six models.

Why it matters: It establishes a theoretical and empirical benchmark for evaluating overthinking, enabling optimized compute allocation during test-time scaling of reasoning models.

entry.title: On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
This paper analyzes continuous diffusion language model design levers, introducing DoubleCat and SemiCat interpolants to eliminate self-conditioning forward passes while matching discrete diffusion performance.

Why it matters: The proposed SemiCat and DoubleCat architectures allow continuous diffusion language models to match or exceed discrete diffusion performance while reducing computational overhead.

entry.title: A Critical Look at Power Sampling when Test Time Sharpening LLMs
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated test-time power sampling for LLM sharpening, discovering that samplers fail to converge and that direct fine-tuning to target power distributions yields inconsistent gains.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that complex MCMC/SMC samplers targeting power distributions can be replaced by simpler Best-of-N selection methods without sacrificing reasoning performance.

entry.title: Multi-Stream Attention Residuals
entry.summary:
Multi-Stream Attention Residuals (MSAR) extends depth-wise Attention Residuals to multi-head depth attention using multi-scale causal convolutions and adaptive mixing without persistent multi-stream memory overhead.

Why it matters: MSAR provides a more compute-efficient residual architecture for large-scale language model pre-training, offering superior loss scaling over prior mechanisms without increasing memory storage costs.

entry.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that task context alters how shared attention heads in language models process graph facts and influence downstream components, using linear response maps to predict post-intervention activation changes.

Why it matters: Measuring task-dependent influence helps explain how models reuse parameters across tasks and enables targeted interventions that modify specific model behaviors without disrupting others.

entry.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
entry.summary:
X-AgentRed is a self-evolving red-teaming framework that uses directed tool-dependency graphs and execution feedback to discover harmful cross-service paths in personal AI agents.

Why it matters: It enables proactive detection of unintended, multi-step security risks and harms in tool-using agents operating across complex software ecosystems.

entry.title: Your Discrete Graph Diffusion Model is Secretly Memorizing
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that unconditional discrete graph diffusion models exhibit conditional memorization, recovering corrupted training graphs far better than test graphs, which cannot be fixed by early stopping without destroying generated graph structure.

Why it matters: Standard unconditional generation metrics mask severe overfitting in discrete GDMs, revealing a fundamental tradeoff where models cannot generate structured graphs without memorizing the training data.

entry.title: ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State
entry.summary:
ReplaySSM unrolls state-space model recurrences to store a periodic checkpoint and an input buffer, avoiding eager state reads/writes at every decoding step.

Why it matters: It alleviates memory bandwidth bottlenecks and quantization errors in hybrid SSM decoding while significantly accelerating speculative decoding pipelines.

entry.title: DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs
entry.summary:
DUALQUANT is a calibration-free post-training weight-and-activation quantization framework that minimizes weight-reconstruction MSE to derive per-channel activation rescalings, achieving hardware-validated speedups.

Why it matters: It enables high-throughput, low-bit LLM inference on modern 4-bit hardware accelerators without requiring pre-run calibration datasets or time-consuming calibration passes.

entry.title: S-Space: Exploring Spatial Workspace in Multimodal Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers identified S-Space, an intrinsic linear representation subspace in multimodal language models where object tokens encode 3D spatial coordinates, serving as an internal spatial workspace for perception, reasoning, and verbal output.

Why it matters: Identifying S-Space exposes the internal mechanisms of MLLM spatial reasoning, pinpointing that spatial failures stem from transformation bottlenecks rather than perception errors.

entry.title: DiffusionART: Efficient, Stable and Scalable Reinforcement of Diffusion Models
entry.summary:
DiffusionART accelerates online RL for diffusion models by aggregating prompt rewards into a shared direction and using a trust-region-masked update, eliminating the need for differentiable reward models or EMA tuning.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces the computational overhead and hyperparameter tuning required to stably fine-tune large-scale image and video diffusion models with black-box rewards.

entry.title: SoftwareGym: Scaling Computer-Use Agent Training with Diverse Synthesized Software Environments
entry.summary:
SoftwareGym is an automated pipeline that synthesizes diverse, runtime-verified GUI software environments to generate scalable training data for computer-use agents.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that automatically synthesized, functional GUI software environments can provide scalable, highly transferable supervision that improves computer-use agent performance on out-of-domain tasks.

entry.title: VisionWeave: Weaving Elastic Visual Representations as a Native Capability of MLLMs
entry.summary:
VisionWeave introduces an end-to-end framework enabling MLLMs to dynamically allocate visual tokens across variable spatial granularities, saving 43.0% of tokens while retaining 98.9% of native performance.

Why it matters: VisionWeave enables significantly faster and lower-cost MLLM inference across images and videos without sacrificing downstream task accuracy.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Learn Their Way to the Top? Evaluating Heuristic Learning in a Long-Running Game Agent Competition
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce Adversarial Heuristic Learning (AHL) and AAArena, a 12-game benchmark evaluating LLM-based agents that iteratively refine game code against human programs without modifying model weights.

Why it matters: AHL demonstrates that LLM agents can autonomously improve complex software and strategy via code iteration rather than compute-intensive weight updating.

entry.title: Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation
entry.summary:
SynthSelf enables effective continual post-training for small models by using a slightly larger same-family aligner to generate high-quality, in-distribution synthetic self-distillation data.

Why it matters: It solves the failure of self-distillation in small language models, enabling them to continually learn new tasks without catastrophic forgetting during on-device deployment.

entry.title: Work2Skill: Capturing Human GUI Experience for Reusable Agent Skill Induction
entry.summary:
Work2Skill is a framework that captures human GUI interactions to induce reusable, context-aware agent skills containing workflow rules, step dependencies, and completion checks.

Why it matters: It improves computer-use agent performance on complex domain-specific tasks by structuring human demonstration data into transferable execution workflows.

entry.title: Contextual Correction of Parallel Draftsfor Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
DCOCO improves speculative decoding by using parallel contextual scoring across adjacent draft positions to restore intra-block dependencies in diffusion-based draft tokens without sequential generation overhead.

Why it matters: It resolves the quality trade-off of non-autoregressive parallel drafting, delivering state-of-the-art inference speedups that persist under heavy concurrent serving loads.

entry.title: InstantFusion: A Shared Latent Interface for Heterogeneous Image Generators
entry.summary:
InstantFusion introduces Latent AutoEncoders to map intermediate denoising states of heterogeneous, frozen image generators into a shared latent space for seamless cross-model transitions.

Why it matters: It enables modular, plug-and-play interoperability between heterogeneous image generators without retraining the underlying frozen models.

entry.title: SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents
entry.summary:
SWE-Duel is a self-scaling evaluation arena where two coding agents evaluate each other in mirrored Red-Blue turns by dynamically creating, verifying, and attempting to repair subtle bugs in real repositories.

Why it matters: By generating and verifying benchmark tasks dynamically at evaluation time, SWE-Duel prevents data contamination and prevents benchmarks from saturating as agent capabilities advance.

entry.title: DataVista: Diagnosing Multimodal LLMs on Data Video Understanding
entry.summary:
DataVista is the first benchmark for evaluating multimodal LLMs on data video understanding, introducing 961 real-world videos and 6,775 questions.

Why it matters: It establishes a standard for evaluating how MLLMs process complex dynamic data visualisations and narrative structure, highlighting key gaps in current reasoning capabilities.

entry.title: Recurrent Harness for Agentic Continual Learning
entry.summary:
ReHarness introduces a recurrent harness framework for agentic continual learning that uses backward revision of textual memory to adapt to distribution shifts in online streaming environments.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agents to continuously learn and adapt to changing environments in streaming scenarios without relying on costly external datasets or off-line fine-tuning.

entry.title: TouchScale: 500 Hours of Human Vision and Touch for Visual-Tactile Learning
entry.summary:
TouchScale is a 500-hour unified visual-tactile dataset featuring synchronized egocentric RGB-D video, wrist RGB video, and dense full-hand bimanual tactile measurements across ~2K predefined tasks.

Why it matters: Scaling visual-tactile human data under a unified sensing setup predictably improves both zero-shot tactile perception and real-world robot manipulation performance.

entry.title: Surfing the Activation Wave: Analyzing the Information and Geometry of LLM Hidden States for Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
A principled framework uses matrix entropy and centered kernel alignment to select informative, non-redundant LLM hidden-state layers for speculative decoding, replacing fixed heuristics.

Why it matters: It replaces empirical trial-and-error heuristics with a dynamic, data-driven methodology for selecting LLM intermediate layers, boosting speculative decoding efficiency.

entry.title: PreSTO: Predictive Subtree Prefetching for Fast LLM Power Sampling
entry.summary:
Predictive SubTree Prefetching (PreSTO) accelerates PowerMH sampling for LLM reasoning by prefetching future Metropolis-Hastings proposals in a batched subtree without changing the original transition kernel.

Why it matters: PreSTO significantly reduces the computational latency of power sampling methods for LLM reasoning without altering the target distribution or approximation accuracy.

entry.title: Adaptive DHiSparse: Speculative Decoding over a Load-Adaptive KV Hierarchy
entry.summary:
Adaptive DHiSparse enables speculative decoding over hierarchical sparse KV caches by dynamically adjusting GPU memory residency based on system load while retaining exact fused retrieval.

Why it matters: It significantly increases serving throughput and concurrency for ultra-long context LLMs within strict latency bounds by optimizing GPU-host KV cache transfers.

entry.title: Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels
entry.summary:
Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization (OAL) groups query-key dimensions by contribution scale to construct a positive quadratic kernel, achieving linear-time attention evaluation while mitigating approximation errors caused by outlier dimensions.

Why it matters: It enables more accurate conversion of pretrained autoregressive models into linear-time transformers by specifically addressing high-impact outlier dimensions during attention linearization.

entry.title: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
entry.summary:
UPTURN improves LLM self-correction by learning where to intervene via a 130K-parameter MLP head and inserting instructions as new user turns rather than inline tokens.

Why it matters: It provides a parameter-efficient, training-free method to significantly improve LLM reasoning accuracy without fine-tuning the base model.

entry.title: AudioTETRIS: Token Elimination via Transitional Importance Signals for Efficient Audio LLMs
entry.summary:
AudioTETRIS is a training-free framework that compresses audio sequence lengths in Large Audio Language Models by fusing encoder representation geometry with attention scores to select top-k tokens across decoder layers.

Why it matters: It enables significantly faster, lower-compute inference for Large Audio Language Models without requiring retraining or auxiliary models.

entry.title: MENTOR: Learning from Failure with On-Policy Pedagogical Intervention
entry.summary:
MENTOR is a plug-and-play multi-agent framework that uses real-time, on-policy pedagogical prompts to diagnose reasoning failures and prevent zero-reward collapse during reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards.

Why it matters: It prevents model training failures on complex tasks by converting unrewarded trajectories into actionable, on-policy learning signals without structural pipeline changes.

entry.title: Defence against the dark arts of distillation: Unsupervised discovery of subliminal learning
entry.summary:
A new unsupervised defence method recovers and suppresses subliminally transferred teacher traits from student language model parameter updates without requiring trait labels or prior knowledge of the trait.

Why it matters: It enables practitioners to audit and remove hidden, unlabelled teacher misalignments from distilled models without needing to know what specific traits were inherited.

entry.title: Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Cross-Teacher Guarding for MOPD (Road MOPD) resolves gradient conflicts and capability degradation in multi-teacher on-policy distillation by using non-routed auxiliary teachers to filter updates via credit assignment and gradient projection.

Why it matters: It prevents joint-optimization degradation when distilling multiple specialized, conflicting expert models into a single student model.

entry.title: Branching On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
BranchOPD improves on-policy distillation by branching trajectories at uncertain decision points and introducing protocol-boundary repair to expand supervision coverage efficiently.

Why it matters: BranchOPD offers a more sample-efficient method for distilling large reasoning and agent models into smaller student models without relying on costly independent trajectory rollouts.

entry.title: Rollout-Time Intervention: Unlocking Agentic Reinforcement Learning Beyond Policy Limits
entry.summary:
Rollout-Time Intervention (RTI) uses reward-side evaluation rubrics during RL rollouts to correct agent errors, generating viable off-policy training trajectories beyond the model's intrinsic exploration capacity.

Why it matters: RTI provides a practical mechanism to train LLM agents on tasks exceeding their initial autonomous exploration capabilities without collapsing during reinforcement learning.

entry.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
entry.summary:
Researchers constructed PyTorch backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks inside host model weights, provably hiding arbitrary computations from capability audits using digital lockers.

Why it matters: The findings establish fundamental cryptographic limits to elicitation-based capability audits, proving that adversaries can reliably conceal dangerous capabilities even during full-access model evaluations.
